scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh:68 - `sed -i ''` only works with macOS sed and fails on GNU/Linux. With GNU sed, `sed -i '' -E "s|...|" file` reads `''` as the script and the substitution as a file name. The command errors out, and `GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL` is never updated, yet the script still prints "Updated". Use a portable form such as `sed -E "s|...|" "$ENV_FILE" > tmp && mv tmp "$ENV_FILE"`. Also, this new dev script is outside the request's scope.

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:1023 - Empty-data updateMany adds a write to every cache refresh and may not bump updatedAt. Every cache refresh now runs `updateMany(..., {})` on all SelectedCalendar rows for the credential. With empty `data`, Prisma may skip the `@updatedAt` bump, so this could be a no-op. Even if it works, the UI never reads it: the cache status comes from `CalendarCache.updatedAt` through `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds`. It also adds a bulk write on the webhook path, and that write can fail the refresh after the cache is already saved. Remove the write, or set `updatedAt: new Date()` explicitly if something actually needs it.

packages/prisma/migrations/20250715160635_add_calendar_cache_updated_at/migration.sql:9 - Hand-added `DEFAULT NOW()` probably doesn't match the Prisma schema, which causes migration drift.. The header comment is the one Prisma writes when it generates a column with no default. This means `schema.prisma` probably declares `updatedAt DateTime @updatedAt` without `@default(now())`, and the `DEFAULT NOW()` was added to the SQL by hand. With that mismatch, the next `prisma migrate dev` sees drift and generates a migration that drops the default. `migrate diff` and drift checks in CI will also flag it. Fix: add `@default(now())` to the field in `schema.prisma` so the schema matches this SQL, and remove the outdated warning comment. I couldn't see the schema.prisma hunk, so this depends on how the field is declared there.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/calendars/deleteCache.handler.ts:24 - Access-denied path throws a plain Error, which tRPC returns as a 500. A missing credential, or one owned by someone else, throws a generic `Error`. tRPC returns that as INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR and logs it as a server fault. Throw `new TRPCError({ code: "NOT_FOUND" })` (or FORBIDDEN) so the client gets the correct error code.

packages/prisma/migrations/20250715160635_add_calendar_cache_updated_at/migration.sql:9 - Backfill makes existing cache rows look freshly updated.. `DEFAULT NOW()` sets `updatedAt` to the migration time for every existing `CalendarCache` row. The new `cacheUpdatedAt` status in the UI will then report every old cache entry as updated at deploy time until the entry is next written, which misstates how fresh it is. A better backfill would use an existing timestamp column, such as `expiresAt` minus the TTL, or would clear the old rows.
